4. **Settings label/value pairs not semantically associated** (settings/page.tsx) — adjacent `<span>`s instead of `<dl>/<dt>/<dd>`; low severity.

findings.title: Reschedule success announces a meaningless label fragment to screen readers
findings.detail: After a successful reschedule the live region announces t("account.nextSession") which resolves to the bare string "Next session" (messages/en.json:362) — a UI label, not a confirmation of what just happened. The reschedule panel also closes (setRescheduleId(null)) and the inputs clear with no visible/announced success state, so a screen-reader user gets no meaningful feedback that the reschedule succeeded. Compare the cancel path on the same component (lines 35-38) which correctly announces a dedicated confirmation message. This is a live-region/feedback gap introduced by this diff.
findings.suggestion: Add a dedicated message (e.g. account.rescheduled = "Booking moved to your new time.") to messages/en.json and announce that instead of t("account.nextSession"). Consider surfacing it via toast(..., "success") for parity with the name-save flow, and move focus back to the booking's action area after the panel closes.

findings.location: Receipts list <a> (lines 183-189) and components/customer/PastSessionsTable.tsx actions column (lines ~44-66)
findings.title: Repeated receipt/rate links share identical accessible names with no per-item context
findings.detail: Every payment row renders an anchor whose entire accessible name is "Download receipt" (t("account.download")), and every past-session row renders "Rate" and "Receipt" links. With more than one row the link list a screen-reader user pulls up is "Download receipt, Download receipt, ..." / "Rate, Receipt, Rate, Receipt, ..." — indistinguishable, so the user cannot tell which booking/listener/date each refers to (WCAG 2.4.4 Link Purpose). axe does not flag duplicate link text, so the existing axe test (single-row) passes despite the problem. The table gives visual row context but the links themselves carry none programmatically.
findings.suggestion: Give each link a distinguishing accessible name, e.g. aria-label built from the row data: `Download receipt for {listenerName}, {dateLabel}` and `Rate your session with {listenerName} on {dateLabel}`. Keep the short visible text but append the context via aria-label (or visually-hidden span).

findings.title: Payment status rendered as raw machine enum, unlocalized and read verbatim
findings.detail: The badge prints p.status directly, so the payment_status enum values "authorized" / "captured" / "refunded" / "failed" (lib/supabase/database.types.ts:634) are shown as-is and spoken verbatim by a screen reader. This is a raw token rather than human-readable copy and violates CLAUDE.md rule 7 (all user-facing strings via messages/en.json) — every other status in the diff (bookings, availability) goes through a localized label map. Additionally a "failed" payment renders with tone="neutral" (grey), so a failure is not visually distinguished from a non-captured-but-fine state; meaning rests on the lowercase token text alone.
findings.suggestion: Add a status->message map (e.g. account.payStatusCaptured / Authorized / Refunded / Failed) and render the localized label. Map "failed" to tone="alert" so the visual treatment matches the meaning and isn't carried by text alone.

findings.location: Settings Card rows, lines ~32-64 (Email / Payment method / Notifications / Language)
findings.title: Label/value setting rows use unassociated spans instead of a description list
findings.detail: Each settings row is two sibling <span>s — a bold label (Email, Payment method, Language) and a value — with no programmatic association between them. A screen reader reads them as adjacent inline text with no name/value relationship, and the order isn't guaranteed to read as a pair. These are textbook definition pairs that should be marked up semantically.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the rows in a <dl> with <dt> for each label and <dd> for each value (the StatusBadge can live inside the <dd>). This conveys the label/value relationship to assistive tech without changing the visual layout.

findings.location: cancel button onClick={() => cancel(item.id)} (lines ~76-83); unused message account.cancelConfirm
findings.title: Destructive cancel executes on a single press with no confirmation step
findings.detail: The Cancel button immediately calls cancelBooking, which can capture/charge the customer's block when cancelled inside the policy window (actions.ts cancelBooking -> payments.capture). The diff even adds an account.cancelConfirm = "Cancel this booking?" message (messages/en.json) but nothing references it (grep finds zero usages). For a blind/low-vision user an accidental activation triggers an irreversible, money-moving action with no guard. This is a safety/usability gap rather than a strict WCAG failure.
findings.suggestion: Gate the cancel behind a confirmation using the existing Dialog primitive (or at minimum a two-step inline confirm) wired to the already-present account.cancelConfirm string, mirroring how other destructive flows confirm before acting.

findings.title: Reschedule success announces a meaningless label fragment to screen readers
findings.detail: After a successful reschedule the live region announces t("account.nextSession") which resolves to the bare string "Next session" (messages/en.json:362) — a UI label, not a confirmation of what just happened. The reschedule panel also closes (setRescheduleId(null)) and the inputs clear with no visible/announced success state, so a screen-reader user gets no meaningful feedback that the reschedule succeeded. Compare the cancel path on the same component (lines 35-38) which correctly announces a dedicated confirmation message. This is a live-region/feedback gap introduced by this diff.
findings.suggestion: Add a dedicated message (e.g. account.rescheduled = "Booking moved to your new time.") to messages/en.json and announce that instead of t("account.nextSession"). Consider surfacing it via toast(..., "success") for parity with the name-save flow, and move focus back to the booking's action area after the panel closes.

findings.location: Receipts list <a> (lines 183-189) and components/customer/PastSessionsTable.tsx actions column (lines ~44-66)
findings.title: Repeated receipt/rate links share identical accessible names with no per-item context
findings.detail: Every payment row renders an anchor whose entire accessible name is "Download receipt" (t("account.download")), and every past-session row renders "Rate" and "Receipt" links. With more than one row the link list a screen-reader user pulls up is "Download receipt, Download receipt, ..." / "Rate, Receipt, Rate, Receipt, ..." — indistinguishable, so the user cannot tell which booking/listener/date each refers to (WCAG 2.4.4 Link Purpose). axe does not flag duplicate link text, so the existing axe test (single-row) passes despite the problem. The table gives visual row context but the links themselves carry none programmatically.
findings.suggestion: Give each link a distinguishing accessible name, e.g. an aria-label built from the row data: `Download receipt for {listenerName}, {dateLabel}` and `Rate your session with {listenerName} on {dateLabel}`. Keep the short visible text but append the context via aria-label or a visually-hidden span.

findings.title: Payment status rendered as raw machine enum, unlocalized and read verbatim
findings.detail: The badge prints p.status directly, so the payment_status enum values "authorized" / "captured" / "refunded" / "failed" (lib/supabase/database.types.ts:634) are shown as-is and spoken verbatim by a screen reader. This is a raw token rather than human-readable copy and violates CLAUDE.md rule 7 (all user-facing strings via messages/en.json) — every other status in the diff (bookings, availability) goes through a localized label map. Additionally a "failed" payment renders with tone="neutral" (grey), so a failure is not visually distinguished from a normal non-captured state; meaning rests on the lowercase token text alone.
findings.suggestion: Add a status->message map (e.g. account.payStatusCaptured / Authorized / Refunded / Failed) and render the localized label. Map "failed" to tone="alert" so the visual treatment matches the meaning and isn't carried by text alone.

findings.location: Settings Card rows, lines ~32-64 (Email / Payment method / Notifications / Language)
findings.title: Label/value setting rows use unassociated spans instead of a description list
findings.detail: Each settings row is two sibling <span>s — a bold label (Email, Payment method, Language) and a value — with no programmatic association between them. A screen reader reads them as adjacent inline text with no name/value relationship, and the pairing isn't conveyed semantically. These are textbook definition pairs that should be marked up as such.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the rows in a <dl> with <dt> for each label and <dd> for each value (the StatusBadge can live inside the <dd>). This conveys the label/value relationship to assistive tech without changing the visual layout.

findings.location: cancel button onClick={() => cancel(item.id)} (lines ~76-83); unused message account.cancelConfirm
findings.title: Destructive cancel executes on a single press with no confirmation step
findings.detail: The Cancel button immediately calls cancelBooking, which can capture/charge the customer's block when cancelled inside the policy window (actions.ts cancelBooking -> payments.capture). The diff even adds an account.cancelConfirm = "Cancel this booking?" message (messages/en.json) but nothing references it (grep finds zero usages). For a blind/low-vision user an accidental activation triggers an irreversible, money-moving action with no guard. This is a safety/usability gap rather than a strict WCAG failure.
findings.suggestion: Gate the cancel behind a confirmation using the existing Dialog primitive (or at minimum a two-step inline confirm) wired to the already-present account.cancelConfirm string, mirroring how other destructive flows confirm before acting.

content.content: Structured output provided successfully

content.text:
I reviewed the M12 customer-dashboard diff (`git diff main...HEAD`) for accessibility issues and reported 5 findings via StructuredOutput. The diff is generally strong on a11y — the shared primitives (DataTable, StatusBadge, Availability, Field, Toast, VoicePlayer, FavoriteButton) all handle labels, aria-pressed, live regions, and semantic markup well. The issues that remain are at the composition layer:

- **Reschedule announces a meaningless fragment** ("Next session") instead of a success confirmation — live-region gap (`components/customer/UpcomingBookings.tsx:55`).
- **Repeated, context-free link names** for receipt/rate links across rows — WCAG 2.4.4 (`app/(customer)/account/page.tsx` receipts + `components/customer/PastSessionsTable.tsx`).
- **Raw payment enum** (`{p.status}`) rendered/spoken verbatim, unlocalized, with "failed" given a neutral grey tone (`app/(customer)/account/page.tsx:177`).
- **Settings label/value pairs** as bare spans instead of a `<dl>` (low).
- **Cancel fires with no confirmation** despite an unused `cancelConfirm` string, for a money-moving action (low).
